# Working Title
TCAC 2.0 — Transformative Change Assessment Corpus 2.0

## Code repo

[Github repository](https://github.com/IPBES-Data/TCAC-2.0)

# Introduction

The literature search for the Transformative Change assessment corpus was conducted using search terms provided by the experts and refined in co-operation with the IPBES task force for data and knowledge management.
The search was conducted using [OpenAlex](https://openalex.org), scripted from [R](https://cran.r-project.org) to use  the [OpenAlex API](https://docs.openalex.org). Search terms for the following searches were defined:

- **Transformative Change**,
- **Nature / Environment**
- **case studies** and 
- **additional search terms** for specific corpora

To assess the quality of the corpus, sets of key papers were selected by the experts to verify if these are in the corpus. 
These key papers were selected per chapter / sub-chapter to ensure that the corpus is representative of each chapter.  

The following terminology is used in this document:

- **Corpus**: A body of works as based on a search on [OpenAlex](https://openalex.org)
- **Transformative Change Assessment Corpus**: Short: TCA corpus; The corpus resulting from the search terms `transformative AND nature`
- **Case corpus**: The corpus resulting from `transformative AND nature AND case`
- **work**: terminology used for a single document in their datasewt. Each work has a unique OpenAlex id, but not necesarily a DOI.

The following searches are conducted on Title and Abstract only as the availability of fulltexts drops in 2020. OpenAlex "inherited" their initial corpus from Microsoft Academic, which contained a many fulltext articles. After that initial start, other sources were used which did not all include fulltext versions. To eliminate a bias towards fulltext articles, we limited the search to abstracts and titles only.

# Results

## Assessment of Search Terms Using OpenAlex

### Number of Hits per Individual Corpus

Number of works returned by each individual search-term query and by
the combined `(nature) AND (transformative change)` query, before and
after the OpenAlex work-type filter is applied (only the types in
`input/openalex_types.csv` with `Included = TRUE` are kept).

```{r}
#| label: hits-per-search-term
cnt <- readRDS(tar_read(count_st))

# pro_request(count_only = TRUE) returns one row per query with `count`
# and `query`; the query column carries the named list element name.
labels <- c(
  tfc_complete = "Transformative Change — all types",
  tfc_filtered = "Transformative Change — filtered",
  nature_complete = "Nature — all types",
  nature_filtered = "Nature — filtered",
  tca_complete = "Assessment Corpus (combined) — all types",
  tca_filtered = "Assessment Corpus (combined) — filtered"
)

dplyr::tibble(
  search = labels[as.character(cnt$query)],
  count = as.integer(cnt$count)
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
    caption = "Number of works matching each search on OpenAlex. *filtered* applies the work-type filter; *all types* does not."
  )
```

The actual TCAC 2.0 corpus extracted from the snapshot (after the
type filter) has:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-corpus-size
n_corpus <- nrow(arrow::open_dataset(tar_read(corpus_tcac20)))
tibble::tibble(`Works extracted` = n_corpus) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

### Key papers in the corpus {#key_papers_in_corpus}

Does the corpus actually cover the works the experts consider key? For
each keypaper we check whether its OpenAlex id is present in the
extracted corpus.

#### Summary

```{r}
#| label: keypapers-in-corpus-summary
kc <- tar_read(keypapers_in_corpus)
tibble::tibble(
  status = c("in corpus", "missing from corpus", "total keypapers"),
  n = c(sum(kc$in_corpus), sum(!kc$in_corpus), nrow(kc)),
  `%` = round(100 * c(mean(kc$in_corpus), mean(!kc$in_corpus), 1), 2)
) |>
  knitr::kable(
    align = c("l", "r", "r"),
    format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
    caption = "Coverage of the keypaper set by the TCAC 2.0 corpus."
  )
```

#### Detail

Per-keypaper presence. Sorted in-corpus first, then by citation. Rows
flagged red are missing from the corpus — candidates for revisiting the
search terms (or the keypaper itself, if it's borderline off-topic).

```{r}
#| label: keypapers-in-corpus-detail
kc |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    status = ifelse(
      in_corpus,
      "<span style='color:green'>in</span>",
      "<span style='color:red'>missing</span>"
    ),
    doi = ifelse(
      is.na(keypaper_doi) | !nzchar(keypaper_doi),
      "",
      sprintf(
        "<a href='https://doi.org/%s' target='_blank'>%s</a>",
        keypaper_doi,
        keypaper_doi
      )
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    status,
    citation = keypaper_citation,
    title = keypaper_title,
    doi
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    escape = FALSE,
    caption = "Per-keypaper presence in the TCAC 2.0 corpus."
  )
```

## TCA Corpus properties


### Publications over time

Bars: yearly count of works in the TCAC 2.0 corpus. Red line:
cumulative proportion of the corpus. Blue line: cumulative proportion
of *all* of OpenAlex over the same year range — a useful baseline for
"is the corpus skewing recent vs the literature as a whole?". Both
cumulative lines use the secondary (right-hand) axis.

```{r}
#| label: publications-over-time
years <- arrow::open_dataset(tar_read(corpus_tcac20)) |>
  dplyr::count(publication_year) |>
  dplyr::collect() |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(publication_year), publication_year >= 1900) |>
  dplyr::arrange(publication_year) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    p = n / sum(n),
    p_cum = cumsum(p)
  )

# OpenAlex universe baseline (from yearly_counts target, label =
# "openalex_universe"). Recompute its cumulative proportion over the
# same year window as the corpus so the two lines are comparable.
oa_universe <- readRDS(tar_read(yearly_counts)) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    label == "openalex_universe",
    publication_year %in% years$publication_year
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(publication_year) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    p_oa = count / sum(count),
    p_oa_cum = cumsum(p_oa)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(publication_year, p_oa, p_oa_cum)

ymax <- max(years$n)

ggplot2::ggplot(years, ggplot2::aes(x = publication_year)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(ggplot2::aes(y = n), fill = "#BBBBBB") +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    ggplot2::aes(y = p_cum * ymax),
    colour = "red",
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = oa_universe,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(y = p_oa_cum * ymax),
    colour = "blue",
    linewidth = 0.9,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Number of works per year (bars)",
    sec.axis = ggplot2::sec_axis(
      ~ . / ymax,
      name = "Cumulative proportion (red = corpus, blue = OpenAlex universe)"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Publication year") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-publications-over-time
years |>
  dplyr::left_join(oa_universe, by = "publication_year") |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(p, p_cum, p_oa, p_oa_cum), \(x) round(x, 4))) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

# Comparison with TCAC 1.0

How does the new TCAC 2.0 corpus differ from TCAC 1.0? Below we compare
the two on three dimensions: works per OpenAlex type, keypaper presence,
and the per-year change in coverage (works added in 2.0 vs works that
were in 1.0 but no longer match in 2.0).

```{r}
#| label: compare-setup
cmp <- tar_read(corpus_comparison)
```

## Works per type

Per OpenAlex `type`, work count in each corpus and the difference
(TCAC 2.0 minus TCAC 1.0). Sorted by TCAC 2.0 count. Negative diff
(works lost) shown in red; positive (works gained) in green.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cmp-types
cmp$type_counts |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    diff = ifelse(
      diff < 0,
      sprintf(
        "<span style='color:red'>%s</span>",
        format(diff, big.mark = ",")
      ),
      sprintf(
        "<span style='color:green'>+%s</span>",
        format(diff, big.mark = ",")
      )
    ),
    `tcac_1.0` = format(`tcac_1.0`, big.mark = ","),
    `tcac_2.0` = format(`tcac_2.0`, big.mark = ",")
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html", escape = FALSE,
    align   = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
    caption = "Works per type in each corpus."
  )
```

## Keypapers in each corpus

For each keypaper, whether the OpenAlex id is present in TCAC 1.0 and /
or in TCAC 2.0. Sorted with "in both" rows at the top.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cmp-keypapers
cmp$keypaper_presence |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    `TCAC 1.0` = ifelse(
      in_tcac10,
      "<span style='color:green'>✓</span>",
      "<span style='color:red'>✗</span>"
    ),
    `TCAC 2.0` = ifelse(
      in_tcac20,
      "<span style='color:green'>✓</span>",
      "<span style='color:red'>✗</span>"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    `TCAC 1.0`, `TCAC 2.0`,
    citation, title
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html", escape = FALSE,
    caption = "Keypaper presence in each corpus."
  )
```

## Publications over time — added, removed, kept

Per-year change in corpus composition between the two extracts.
*Added* (green, above zero) = works present in TCAC 2.0 but not in
TCAC 1.0. *Removed* (red, below zero, drawn as negative counts so the
visual is symmetric) = works present in TCAC 1.0 but not in TCAC 2.0.
*Both* (grey backdrop) = works present in both — included to show the
scale of the carried-over base, not the change.

```{r}
#| label: fig-cmp-yearly
ys <- cmp$yearly_status |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from  = status,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0L
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    removed = `removed (only in TCAC 1.0)`,
    both    = `both`,
    added   = `added (only in TCAC 2.0)`
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(removed_neg = -removed)

ggplot2::ggplot(ys, ggplot2::aes(x = publication_year)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    ggplot2::aes(y = both, fill = "both"),
    width = 1, alpha = 0.35
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    ggplot2::aes(y = added, fill = "added (only in TCAC 2.0)"),
    width = 1
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(
    ggplot2::aes(y = removed_neg, fill = "removed (only in TCAC 1.0)"),
    width = 1
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
    name   = NULL,
    breaks = c(
      "added (only in TCAC 2.0)",
      "both",
      "removed (only in TCAC 1.0)"
    ),
    values = c(
      "added (only in TCAC 2.0)"   = "#59A14F",
      "both"                       = "#999999",
      "removed (only in TCAC 1.0)" = "#E15759"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = \(x) format(abs(x), big.mark = ",")) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Publication year",
    y = "Number of works"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cmp-yearly-summary
cmp$yearly_status |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = sum(n), .by = status) |>
  dplyr::mutate(`%` = round(100 * n / sum(n), 2)) |>
  knitr::kable(
    format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
    caption = sprintf(
      "Aggregate composition of the corpus change. TCAC 1.0: %s works; TCAC 2.0: %s works.",
      format(cmp$n_tcac10, big.mark = ","),
      format(cmp$n_tcac20, big.mark = ",")
    )
  )
```
